tweets: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur — begun in 1117 CE by the Hoysala king Viṣṇuvardhana, said to have taken 103 years to complete. Its walls are soapstone: soft from the quarry for the finest chisel work, hardening only with age.

Among its lathe-turned pillars stands the Narasimha column, carved so precisely it once rotated on its own base — until custodians stopped the spinning to spare the stone. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history
